title: A colorimetric technique to characterize mass transfer during liquid-liquid slug flow in circular capillaries
author: Liu, Yao, et al.

steps.title: Install capillary in immersion pool
steps.instruction: Insert the capillary tube through the immersion pool, straighten it, and tighten it at both ends of the PMMA plate with fittings and ferrules, leaving at least 5 cm of capillary protruding from one end for later connection to a Y/T‑junction.

steps.title: Connect capillary to T‑junction and outlet
steps.instruction: Connect one end of the capillary to the T‑junction (inlets 1 and 2 for organic and aqueous phases) and leave the opposite end as outlet 1.

steps.title: Attach PTFE tubes and fill continuous phase
steps.instruction: Connect the immersion‑pool liquid‑delivery tunnel to PTFE tubes (using metal screws and nuts) as inlet 3 and outlet 2, fill a syringe with n‑octane (continuous phase) and slowly inject it through inlet 3 to expel gas bubbles from the pool.

steps.title: Seal immersion pool and position optics
steps.instruction: Lift the immersion pool so that inlet 3 and outlet 2 face upward, remove the two screws, insert a blind ferrule into each, and tighten the screws to prevent n‑octane leakage; then place the assembled PMMA plate and capillary between the back‑light and the high‑speed camera (mounted on the microscope).

steps.title: Set camera magnification and focus
steps.instruction: Set the microscope magnification to ×2.0 (resolution 0.0071 mm pixel⁻¹), adjust the high‑speed camera to focus on the centre‑plane of the capillary, yielding a view area of 81 × 1280 pixels, and keep the whole assembly motion‑free for the entire experiment.

steps.title: Prepare stock solutions A, B, C
steps.instruction: Prepare three stock solutions: Solution A – 0.6 g L⁻¹ resazurin; Solution B – 80 g L⁻¹ glucose; Solution C – 80 g L⁻¹ NaOH. Store all solutions in sealed reagent bottles; keep Solution B refrigerated to suppress microbial activity.

steps.title: Set up magnetic stirrer
steps.instruction: Place a 150 mL beaker containing a magnetic stir bar onto a magnetic stirrer and set the rotation speed to 500 r min⁻¹.

steps.title: Mix designated resazurin solution
steps.instruction: According to Table 2, pipette the listed volumes of deionised water, Solution A, and 20 mL of Solution B into the beaker, then add 20 mL of Solution C drop‑by‑drop (Solution C must be added slowly). The designated solutions are:

substeps.instruction: i (blank): 400 mL water, 20 mL A, 20 mL B, 20 mL C
ii (0.040 g L⁻¹): 34.7 mL water, 5 mL A, 20 mL B, 20 mL C
iii (0.100 g L⁻¹): 26.7 mL water, 13 mL A, 20 mL B, 20 mL C
iv (0.200 g L⁻¹): 13.3 mL water, 26 mL A, 20 mL B, 20 mL C
v (0.260 g L⁻¹): 5.3 mL water, 34 mL A, 20 mL B, 20 mL C
vi (0.300 g L⁻¹): 0 mL water, 40 mL A, 20 mL B, 20 mL C

steps.title: Reduce solution to light green
steps.instruction: Using a syringe, draw approximately 25 mL (≈½ of the syringe range) of the freshly prepared designated solution, let it rest until the colour changes to light green (≈15 min).

steps.title: Calibrate by air oxidation
steps.instruction: Block inlet 1, fill the syringe completely with ambient air, shake to mix air and liquid, then discharge the gas phase; repeat the fill‑shake‑discharge cycle at least three times until the solution turns pink (fully oxidised), immediately inject the solution into the capillary setup and start image recording. Repeat steps 2–5 for each designated solution.

steps.title: Prepare air‑saturated organic phase
steps.instruction: Unblock the inlet for the organic phase, draw air‑saturated n‑octane into a glass syringe and connect the syringe to inlet 1.

steps.title: Prepare designated solution vi for experiment
steps.instruction: Prepare the vi‑designated solution (0.300 g L⁻¹ resazurin) following steps 2–3, fill a syringe with the solution, connect it to the experimental setup as soon as possible, and let the liquid rest until it becomes light green. Ensure the fully‑reduced solution is used within 1 h to avoid side‑reaction colour changes; the syringe volume can be estimated from the flow rate and the ≤1 h runtime.

steps.title: Inject liquids and record images
steps.instruction: Using syringe pumps, inject both the air‑saturated n‑octane (organic phase) and the reduced aqueous solution into the capillary microreactor, then record the slug‑flow images with the previously set‑up high‑speed camera system.
